Trace: beadrs-cf4b2115 revision 13 and beadrs-7ee540ac revision 13 both recorded actionable rejection for absent or underspecified Q truth-table, maximal word-run and m semantics, identifier shape/tokenization, and exclusion coverage. The current fixture commit 46f8fc2ab744b6b52aa5fb08a992ae50907fd1a7 changes the evidence only: it supplies Q witness rows and local assignment-name exclusions, not a complete identifier contract. No secret-ruleset-v4 normative source or other implementation was inspected.

Compatibility rationale: ADR-014 requires offline deterministic findings, raw field byte ranges, and exact-fingerprint acknowledgement. ADR-023 item 5 requires an integer Q qualifier for labelled assignments and refers to an excluded-identifier list. ADR-025 names hexadecimal digest lengths, UUIDs, generation identifiers, and bead identifiers as unlabelled advisory exclusions. secret-rejection-v1 sections 2, 3, and 6 require deterministic findings, byte ranges, closed rule behavior, and required conformance coverage. needle-cli-contract-v1 requires a returned bead_id and opaque issue IDs but defines no ID grammar. The independent Q fixture passes eight tests and explicitly witnesses maximal word runs, strict integer boundaries, and case/separator name exclusions. It does not give scanner verdicts or byte spans for an actual bead-0123456789abcdef ID, UUID, generation-unknown-fields-v1, or digest-shaped values. Its bead_identifier witness is ticket-3a3a3a3a, and its excluded() helper applies to assignment names rather than the value-shape exclusions named by ADR-025. The attempt and unknown-fields fixtures provide examples such as bead-0123456789abcdef, bead-unknown-a, generation-unknown-fields-v1, and a UUID, but do not define secret-scan outcomes.

Threat-model impact: unresolved Q boundaries can false-negative labelled credentials or false-positive ordinary values; unresolved exclusions can either permit credential-like text to evade blocking or reject routine IDs and create mutation denial of service, eroding trust in the gate. Divergent raw spans or identifier classification also change fingerprints and can make acknowledgement or redaction miss the stored bytes. This is material under ADR-014 because accepted mutations publish to the checkpoint and may reach a public mirror.

Concrete blocker and required synthetic coverage: publish a normative, versioned definition of byte versus character scope, maximal word-run precedence, every Q inequality and m value, assignment-label versus value scope, and exact exclusion grammar/boundaries. Add value-level expected verdict rows for 32/40/64-hex digests, UUIDs, generation IDs, actual bead IDs, near misses, and the same values beside a provider-formatted credential rule to prove exclusions are local. Add Q pass/fail boundary rows, placeholder rows, labelled versus unlabelled rows, Unicode byte-span rows, and deterministic fingerprint/range assertions. Acceptance basis is a passing fixture suite tied to that definition; the present fixture suite is evidence for Q witnesses only, not acceptance of the overall finding.

No repository source, test, config, or documentation files were changed and no commit was created; unrelated concurrent worktree changes were preserved. Per-section verdicts:
- Result envelope and output: PASS. Text success is exactly one comment ID line; JSON success envelopes have the documented operation/id/issue_id/author/resolution fields, reply_to_id and previous_resolution_state presence rules, semantic_change and workspace_sequence; bodies are absent. Dry-run always emits JSON and commits no rows/events. Diagnostics stayed on stderr and failure stdout was empty. Advisory secret_scan is added only when advisory findings exist; off mode omits it.
- Secret-scan interaction: PARTIAL/DIVERGENCE. Native and disposable org-scanner blocking findings rejected whole comment writes atomically, emitted secret_detected diagnostics without matched bytes, and left rows/events unchanged. Advisory committed with stderr notice and envelope summary; off committed with no scan member. Exact fingerprint admission committed and produced a secret_acknowledged audit event. The spec sentence requiring an “acknowledgment audit” for advisory mode was not observed as a durable acknowledgment row/event; only exact admission produced that event.
- Exit codes: PARTIAL/DIVERGENCE. Observed: body-file transport I/O 1; usage/empty/oversize/unknown/near-miss 2; missing workspace/issue 3; bad/cross-issue target and quarantine gate 4; blocking native/org secret rejection 2; SQLite lock contention 1. The documented invalid-UTF-8=4 and database-busy=6 results did not match shipped behavior.

1 Create — REPRODUCIBLE/PASS: ID-only stdout, comment- prefix, worker author, unresolved state, comment_added event.
2 Reply — REPRODUCIBLE/PASS: reply_to_id and event detail carried both IDs.
3 Resolution transitions — REPRODUCIBLE/PASS: resolve/unresolve events, repeat resolve exit 0 with semantic_change=false and no event.
4 Import compatibility — REPRODUCIBLE/PASS: fixture comment with NULL state; unresolve no-op with previous_resolution_state null, resolve writes explicit resolved with previous null.
5 Bad reply target — REPRODUCIBLE/PASS: missing and cross-issue targets exit 4 with no stdout/state change.
6 Missing selectors — REPRODUCIBLE/PASS: missing issue exits 3 with Issue <id> not found and no state change.
7 Body transport — REPRODUCIBLE with DIVERGENCE: neither/both exit 2, stdin stores the exact newline-bearing body, unreadable input exits 1, empty/whitespace exits 2; invalid UTF-8 stdin exited 1 rather than documented 4.
8 Scan outcomes — REPRODUCIBLE with DIVERGENCE: enforce rejects native and org findings at exit 2 rather than comment spec exit 4; advisory/off behavior and redaction of matched bytes pass; advisory durable acknowledgment wording did not match observed state.
9 Projection defaults — REPRODUCIBLE/PASS: show default has no bodies; --comments all returns canonical body-bearing rows; receipts/envelopes omit bodies.
10 Checkpoint round trip — REPRODUCIBLE/PASS: flush/import into a fresh workspace restored comment rows/events; retained secret findings were reported without preventing recovery, and quarantine was established.
11 Revision independence — REPRODUCIBLE/PASS: comment writes left parent revision and updated_at unchanged.
12 Shared gates — REPRODUCIBLE for recovery-quarantine subcase: comment write exited 4 with no stdout/state change. Maintenance-hold subcase was not reproducible without manufacturing an interrupted redaction publication state; no claim is made for that subcase.

Full spec-side amendment text for every divergence:

AMENDMENT A — research/specs/comment-mutation-v1.md, “Validation rules” V6; “Exit codes”; Conformance scenario 7:
“Body-file/stdin input whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 is a transport I/O failure. It exits 1, writes no JSON envelope or comment/event/checkpoint state, and reports a value-free I/O diagnostic on stderr. Replace the V6 invalid-UTF-8 exit from 4 to 1; remove invalid UTF-8 from exit 4’s conflict/validation instances; and change Conformance scenario 7 to require exit 1.”

AMENDMENT B — research/specs/comment-mutation-v1.md, “Result envelope and output”, “Secret-scan interaction”, “Exit codes”, and Conformance scenario 8, harmonizing with secret-rejection-v1:
“An unacknowledged blocking secret finding rejects the complete request before the semantic write transaction with exit 2 and no stdout envelope, in both human and --json modes. The stderr reason remains secret_detected and must not contain matched bytes. Remove blocking secret_detected from exit 4’s instances and add it to exit 2’s CLI usage/argument-validation instances. Conformance scenario 8 requires exit 2, not exit 4. Exit 4 remains for referenced-record conflicts and shared maintenance/quarantine refusals.”

AMENDMENT C — research/specs/comment-mutation-v1.md, “Secret-scan interaction”, modes/outcomes and Conformance scenario 8:
“Advisory mode writes the comment and emits the standard value-free advisory line plus the secret_scan envelope summary. It does not create an acknowledgment audit event; a secret_acknowledged event is created only when an exact fingerprint is explicitly admitted by --acknowledge-secret or secret_scan.acknowledged. Off mode emits neither scan notice nor additive envelope member.”

AMENDMENT D — research/specs/comment-mutation-v1.md, “Exit codes” and Conformance scenario 12/lock behavior:
“SQLite write-lock contention observed by a comment command is reported through the shipped generic SQLite/internal error path and exits 1. The comment-command contract does not promise a distinct exit-6 busy result unless the CLI error ladder is changed; remove database busy from exit 6 for this command and classify it under exit 1 pending a separately shipped busy-code contract.”

Operational note: the first disposable directory was nested below an existing shared scratch .beads store; discovery was stopped, the one accidentally-created temporary issue was removed by verified restore of the pre-probe checkpoint, and no live repository store was touched. Creates a new issue with the specified title and optional metadata.
The issue ID is automatically generated and printed on success.
Fresh creates print only the issue ID followed by a newline; idempotent
reference hits use the explicit result prefixes described below.

IDEMPOTENT CREATION:
  --unique-ref NAMESPACE:KEY atomically binds a stable external identity.
  A repeated create returns `EXISTING ID`; a repeated create whose binding
  points to a closed issue returns `EXISTING_CLOSED ID` so callers can stop
  retrying finished work.

PRIORITIES:
  0 = urgent (immediate incident, safety, or release-blocking)
  1 = critical (essential work preceding ordinary delivery)
  2 = high (important planned work, default)
  3 = normal (ordinary work with no elevated urgency)
  4 = aspirational/backlog (speculative or low-urgency work)

EXAMPLES:
  bead create --title "Fix authentication bug" --priority 0
  bead create --title "Update documentation" --priority 2 --label docs
  bead create --title "Build image" --resource-key docker:daemon --resource-key gpu:0
  bead create --title "Materialize tracker work" --unique-ref github:issue-123
  bead create --title "Add search feature" --assignee alice --label feature --label backend
  bead create --title "Code review PR-123" --description "Review changes for user auth"

ISSUE TYPES:
  Common types include: task, bug, feature, improvement, documentation
  Custom types can be specified as needed (no validation is performed).

RESOURCE KEYS:
  --resource-key declares a normalized, case-sensitive key used only for
  scheduling exclusion inside this native workspace. It is not a distributed
  lock. Claims acquire every declared key atomically; release, close, and
  expired leases return keys. Use `bead resource add|remove|list` after create.

Usage: bead create [OPTIONS] --title <TITLE>

Options:
      --no-auto-flush
          Suppress automatic post-commit checkpoint publication for this one invocation, leaving the checkpoint dirty for a later explicit `bead sync flush-only`; overrides the `checkpoint.auto_flush` workspace configuration key

      --title <TITLE>
          Issue title (required)

      --acknowledge-secret <FINGERPRINT>
          Admit only findings whose exact scanner fingerprint matches this value. Repeat for multiple findings. Every successful mutation using an acknowledgment records a same-transaction audit event; there is no blanket bypass flag

      --description <DESCRIPTION>
          Issue description (optional, defaults to empty)

      --priority <PRIORITY>
          Issue priority (0-4, default: 2)
          
          [default: 2]

      --skip-foreign-workspace
          Let workspace discovery continue past the first `.beads` directory when it is not a bead-rs workspace (no `.beads/config.json`), so a bead-rs workspace farther up the tree can be used. Discovery otherwise stops there and fails closed: it never silently skips a `.beads` it does not recognize to operate on an unrelated parent workspace, and it never writes into the unrecognized directory -- including under this flag, which only widens the search

      --issue-type <ISSUE_TYPE>
          Issue type (default: task)

      --assignee <ASSIGNEE>
          Assignee (optional)

      --label <LABEL>
          Labels to add (can be specified multiple times)

      --resource-key <RESOURCE_KEYS>
          Workspace-local resource key (can be specified multiple times)

      --unique-ref <UNIQUE_REF>
          Idempotency binding in NAMESPACE:KEY form

  -h, --help
